title: Cartesian fibration over a groupoid completion
statement: Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Inner fibration has the inner-horn lifting meaning of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. In this statement a Cartesian fibration $p:X\to Y$ means an inner fibration admitting a lift $x'\to x$ of every arrow $y'\to p(x)$ with specified target, such that for every $z\in X$ the square $\operatorname{Map}_X(z,x')\to\operatorname{Map}_X(z,x)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_Y(pz,y')\to\operatorname{Map}_Y(pz,px)$ is a homotopy pullback. For a small infinity-category $W$, choose a Kan fibrant replacement $\eta:W\to\kappa W$ in the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]: $\kappa W$ is a Kan complex and $\eta$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Such a replacement exists in the same universe; it is called the groupoid completion. Let $\pi:\mathcal F\to\kappa W$ be a Cartesian fibration and form the pullback $\mathcal F'=W\times_{\kappa W}\mathcal F$ in infinity-categories. Then restriction along $\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F$ identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal F,\mathcal T)$ with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal F',\mathcal T)$ on functors carrying every arrow whose image in $\mathcal F$ is an equivalence to an equivalence, including all mapping spaces, for every target infinity-category $\mathcal T$ in a sufficiently large universe.

source.place: Definition 5.3.11 and Lemma 5.3.15. Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical theorem.

proof.text: To see existence, factor $W\to\Delta^0$ in the universe-relative functorial Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] as a trivial cofibration $W\to\kappa W$ followed by a Kan fibration $\kappa W\to\Delta^0$. This supplies a groupoid completion in the same universe. The argument below applies to the chosen $\eta$: it uses only its weak homotopy equivalence property and Kan target. Work in a universe containing $W,\kappa W,\mathcal F$ and the chosen target; use a further universe for categories of diagrams. Thus the smallness hypotheses of classification and colimit theorems do not impose an extra bound on $\mathcal F$. For a quasicategory $\mathcal D$ and vertices $x,y$, [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] gives natural homotopy equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(x,y)\simeq U_{\mathcal D}(x,y)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}}(y,x)\simeq U_{\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}}(y,x)$; the latter arrow space is $U_{\mathcal D}(x,y)^{\mathrm{op}}$ by the isomorphism $\Delta^1\cong(\Delta^1)^{\mathrm{op}}$, and reversing barycentric coordinates (step 3) identifies its realization with that of $U_{\mathcal D}(x,y)$. These identifications are natural in simplicial functors, so mapping-space squares in $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{op}}$ over $(\kappa W)^{\mathrm{op}}$ are the opposite squares of $\mathcal F$ over $\kappa W$. Hence the opposite of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] identifies the mapping-pullback Cartesian condition in the statement with the horn condition of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations].

source.place: Lemma 5.3.15, proof: classifying functors of the fibration and its pullback; Theorem 3.2.0.1 and Remark 2.4.1.12; supporting Higher Topos Theory results as specified

proof.text: With the mapping and horn Cartesian conventions identified in step 1, apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] to opposites to classify $\pi$ by $F:(\kappa W)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$. Explicitly apply cocartesian straightening to $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{op}}\to(\kappa W)^{\mathrm{op}}$ and then take the opposite of each value and transport. Its base-change clause classifies $\pi'$ by $F\circ\eta^{\mathrm{op}}$. The base-change clause of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], applied to opposites, also identifies the simplicial pullback with the infinity-categorical pullback. By [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus] this pullback is Cartesian and its Cartesian edges are precisely those mapping to $\pi$-Cartesian edges.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.15, proof: classifying functors of the fibration and its pullback; Theorem 3.2.0.1 and Remark 2.4.1.12; supporting Higher Topos Theory results as specified

proof.text: The simplicial opposite reverses the barycentric coordinates of every geometric simplex; these reversals identify the realizations of a simplicial set and its opposite and commute with realization of maps. Consequently $u=\eta^{\mathrm{op}}:A=W^{\mathrm{op}}\to K=(\kappa W)^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence and $K$ is Kan. For $k\in K$, apply [lem-coef-space-path-fibration-replacement] to $\{k\}\to K$: the source-fixed path space $P_k=\{k\}\times_{K,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,K)$ has a Kan fibration $\operatorname{ev}_1:P_k\to K$ and the constant-path inclusion $\Delta^0\to P_k$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Right properness in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] now gives a weak homotopy equivalence $P_k\times_K A\to P_k$, as the pullback of $u$ along that Kan fibration. Thus $P_k\times_K A$ is weakly contractible. This is exactly the arrow-comma model $(k\downarrow u)$ in [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test], whose implication (3) to (1) says restriction takes every colimiting cocone to a colimiting cocone. Apply it to $F:K\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ in the enlarged universe; $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ has small colimits by [lem-coef-infinity-functor-pushout], so $F$ and $Fu$ have colimit cocones, and the colimit cocone of $F$ restricts to a colimit cocone on $Fu$. Hence the canonical comparison $c:\operatorname{colim}_{W^{\mathrm{op}}}(F\circ\eta^{\mathrm{op}})\to\operatorname{colim}_{(\kappa W)^{\mathrm{op}}}F$ is an equivalence. The comma-contractibility calculation is a direct application of the two cited path-space/model-structure statements and needs no new cofinality node.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.15, proof: cofinality and equality of colimits; Corollary 4.1.2.6, Theorem 4.1.3.1 and Proposition 4.1.1.8; supporting Higher Topos Theory results as specified

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cartesian-colimit-localization] to $\pi$ and $\pi'$. Write $L=\operatorname{colim}F$ and $L'=\operatorname{colim}(F\circ\eta^{\mathrm{op}})$. It supplies $\ell:\mathcal F\to L$ and $\ell':\mathcal F'\to L'$ localizing at the respective Cartesian edges, with the whole functor-category universal properties. If $r:\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F$ is the projection, the natural comparison is $c\ell'\simeq\ell r$. This fixes the actual projection in the localization comparison; it is stronger than an unrelated equivalence between two abstract colimit objects.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.15, proof: colimit of each classifying diagram is its Cartesian-edge localization; Corollary 3.3.4.3; supporting Higher Topos Theory results as specified

proof.text: Use the associative and unital mapping-space composition classes and their equivalence-edge characterization from [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. For an edge $a:x\to y$ of $\mathcal F$, postcomposition by $\pi(a)$ has postcomposition by an inverse edge as a homotopy inverse on every base mapping space, because $\kappa W$ is Kan: the two outer horns in dimension two give left and right homotopy inverses of any edge. If $a$ is Cartesian, its defining homotopy-pullback square therefore makes $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F}(z,x)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F}(z,y)$ an equivalence for every $z$. Taking $z=y$ produces $b:y\to x$ with $ab\simeq1_y$; taking $z=x$ and using injectivity on components then gives $ba\simeq1_x$. Thus $a$ is an equivalence. Conversely if $a$ is an equivalence, both horizontal maps of this square are equivalences, so the square is a homotopy pullback. Hence $\mathrm{Cart}(\pi)=\operatorname{Eq}(\mathcal F)$. The localization $\ell$ of step 4 is an equivalence: every functor already inverts equivalences. More explicitly its universal property with target $\mathcal F$ gives $h:L\to\mathcal F$ with $h\ell\simeq1$; full faithfulness of restriction with target $L$ gives $\ell h\simeq1$ after precomposing by $\ell$. The inverse criterion here is the homotopy-category definition of equivalence in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Lemma 5.3.15, proof: Cartesian edges over a Kan base are exactly equivalences; the mapping-space proof of Proposition 2.4.1.5; supporting Higher Topos Theory results as specified

proof.text: By the base-change edge assertion of [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus], an edge $a'$ of $\mathcal F'$ is $\pi'$-Cartesian exactly when $r(a')$ is $\pi$-Cartesian. Step 5 identifies the latter condition with $r(a')$ being an equivalence in $\mathcal F$. Thus the system inverted by $\ell'$ in step 4 is exactly the system requested in the statement, with no extra requirement that the image edge in $W$ be an equivalence.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.15, proof: last sentence, identification of edges in the pullback; Remark 2.4.1.12 and Remark 2.4.2.13; supporting Higher Topos Theory results as specified

proof.text: For every target $\mathcal T$, precomposition along the equivalences $c:L'\to L$ of step 3 and $\ell:\mathcal F\to L$ of step 5 gives equivalences of functor infinity categories. The natural equivalence $c\ell'\simeq\ell r$ of step 4 identifies their composites with restriction $r^*$. The universal property of $\ell'$ therefore identifies $r^*$ with the full subcategory of functors on $\mathcal F'$ inverting the system in step 6. Since the universal property in [lem-coef-cartesian-colimit-localization] is for whole functor categories, this includes noninvertible transformations and every mapping space, as required.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.15, proof: assemble the localization universal property; supporting Higher Topos Theory results as specified
